profile.headline: Software Engineer | Embedded Systems · IoT · Real-Time Software | C++ · Python · Linux | Origin AI · Honeywell · NASA
profile.summary:
Software Engineer with 7+ years of experience building production embedded systems, real-time engines, and automated tooling for mission-critical applications.
At Origin AI I work on the AI Engines team developing WiFi CSI-based sensing software in C++ and C on Linux. I own the Sensing Health Check engine end-to-end, most recently leading the full design, implementation, and release of SHC 2.0, a continuous device health monitoring system shipped May 2026. I also drive debugging infrastructure, automated tooling, and cross-team technical collaboration.

Before Origin AI, I spent 4.5 years at Honeywell engineering avionics and defense software leading an RTOS-to-POSIX migration, integrating the military VICTORY framework, and building an automated testing tool that cut project delivery time by 38%. Prior to that I interned at NASA Kennedy Space Center on Artemis 1 Launch Control and NASA Glenn Research Center on International Space Station systems.

Core stack: C++ · C · Python · Bash · Linux · RTOS/POSIX · WiFi CSI · TCP/UDP · HTTP POST · MQTT · CoAP · libcoap · MIL-STD-1553B · CMake · Make · Docker · ESP32 · ARM · Git · Agile

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Production embedded development for WiFi CSI-based environment sensing. Responsible for designing, implementing and testing engine architecture, signal processing pipelines, and automated testing infrastructure. Core stack: C++, C, Python, Bash, and Linux.

• Owned end-to-end design, implementation, testing, and release of Sensing Health Check 2.0, a multi-mode WiFi device vetting engine shipped May 2026 across three repositories.

• Redesigned SHC from a single-mode diagnostic tool into a continuous monitoring service, enabling long-term device health tracking for the first time and laying the groundwork for parallel mode execution.

• Led the testing effort for SHC 2.0: smoke, unit, regression, integration, and a 12-hour AddressSanitizer stress run with zero crashes.

• Achieved 80–85% CPU improvement on Speed Engine while maintaining alignment with the R&D MATLAB reference engine.

• Established ARM-target debugging infrastructure including cross-compiled AddressSanitizer and remote GDB debugging on embedded hardware.

• Redesigned the CSI Saving engine's driver integration layer into a unified manager capable of handling multiple driver types and CSI formats, and contributed to API redesign efforts.

• Built automated tooling that eliminated recurring build and test setup friction for engineers across multiple teams.

• Mentored a QA engineer in embedded C++ and onboarded a web intern to the embedded architecture.

• Received Kudos of the Month (Oct 2025) for reliability and cross-team support.

positions.title: Personal goal pursuit
positions.description:
I took a well-deserved break from traditional employment to prioritize my mental well-being, and delve into exciting new technologies.

During this enriching period, I:

• Prioritized mental health and personal well-being: Recognizing the importance of self-care, I invested time in activities that nurtured my mental and emotional health. This allowed me to return to the workforce feeling refreshed and energized.

• Embraced technological exploration: I immersed myself in the world of Flutter, APIs, machine learning, LLM AI models and generative AI models, expanding my skillset and gaining valuable knowledge. This newfound expertise opens up exciting possibilities for future career endeavors.

• Explored the potential of LLMs: I actively explored the capabilities of large language models and how they can be applied to coding, designing and streamlining daily tasks. This newfound understanding equips me to work smarter and more efficiently.

• Pursued passive income opportunities: I explored various avenues to generate passive income for my family, laying the groundwork for a more financially secure future. This demonstrates my initiative and proactiveness.

positions.title: Software Engineer II
positions.description:
Embedded navigation software development for the eTALIN guidance and navigation system, deployed across military and commercial land platforms worldwide.

• Led a 6–8 month RTOS-to-POSIX migration of the eTALIN embedded navigation system, replacing the entire RTOS library stack and rebuilding all OS-dependent components, expanding deployment flexibility across new hardware environments and enabling support for new customer platforms.

• Integrated the VICTORY real-time communication framework into eTALIN, enabling coordinated data exchange between vehicle sensors and onboard computers and unlocking support for new customers and platforms.

• Designed and implemented a remote sensor data collection tool that eliminated the need to fly engineers to customer sites for data capture, reducing travel costs and increasing data availability for the engineering team.

• Mentored 2 software engineers and multiple interns in embedded C++, system design, and codebase onboarding.

• Developed and maintained embedded software for a navigation platform with 25,000+ units deployed across 60+ military and commercial platforms worldwide.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.locationName: Aguadilla, Puerto Rico, Puerto Rico · On-site
positions.description:
Embedded software development across multiple mission-critical guidance and navigation programs.

• Developed an automated aviation performance test pipeline reducing engineer workload by 38%, replacing a week-long manual process with a single automated system that ran MATLAB tests, collected and organized results, generated summary reports, and reported status to Atlassian Bamboo and Jira.

• Contributed to the F-35 guidance and navigation system Ada-to-C++ codebase migration, a large-scale multi-team effort rebuilding thousands of lines of mission-critical software with additional improvements.

• Developed features and tests for the ULA Vulcan rocket guidance and navigation system, recognized by the program lead for thoroughness and reliability across deliverables.

• Contributed to guidance and navigation software across multiple platforms including the F-35, ULA Vulcan rocket, and KAI helicopter programs, working across C, C++, and Ada codebases.

• Inherited, improved, and expanded Frida-based dynamic instrumentation integration test infrastructure, building new tests, fixing existing ones, and identifying bugs across the test suite.

• Implemented networking features and tests across TCP, UDP, ICMP, and MIL-STD-1553B protocols on multiple embedded platforms.

positions.locationName: Kennedy Space Center, Florida, United States
positions.description:
At NASA's Kennedy Space Center, I collaborated with my intern partner on pioneering initiatives to advance telemetry data inspection, optimize system diagrams, and drive software development lifecycle integration. Leveraging Python and Unix-based systems, we contributed to the creation of cutting-edge TCP and UDP features for telemetry emulation. Key Contributions:

• Enhanced system diagrams for software upgrades
• Coordinated integration of software development lifecycle
• Executed comprehensive software emulation testing
• Authored developers' guide for future improvements
• Implemented Agile methodologies for rapid project deliveries

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.locationName: Glenn Research Center, Ohio, United States
positions.description:
At NASA's Glenn Research Center, I played a pivotal role in advancing software engineering initiatives, ensuring mission success through meticulous attention to detail and innovation. Leveraging expertise in C++, Qt framework, and an array of software tools, I engineered mission-critical features, aligning closely with project specifications. My proactive approach to software development included the implementation of automated unit tests, effectively identifying and rectifying bugs and defects. Spearheading the design and execution of automated tests for diverse systems including FTP communication, hardware, sensors, and core platforms, I contributed to the enhancement of overall system reliability and performance. Collaborating closely with stakeholders, I coordinated embedded software tests in laboratory environments, consistently meeting customer objectives and exceeding expectations. By seamlessly integrating quality tests into Atlassian tools' Bamboo automated testing environment, I ensured robustness and efficiency in software validation processes. My dedication to quality assurance was further demonstrated through the detection and resolution of multiple software escapes, fostering continuous improvement and excellence in software functionality. 

Key Contributions:

• Engineered mission-critical features using C++, Qt framework, and various software tools.
• Streamlined software development through automated unit tests, addressing bugs and defects efficiently.
• Led the creation of automated tests for FTP communication, hardware, sensors, and core platform systems.
• Coordinated embedded software tests in laboratory settings, ensuring customer satisfaction.
• Integrated quality tests into Atlassian tools' Bamboo automated testing environment.
• Detected and resolved multiple software escapes, enhancing software quality and functionality.

positions.title: Laboratory Assistant
positions.description:
During my internship at Clemson University as a Laboratory Assistant, I played a pivotal role in various cutting-edge projects, showcasing my adeptness in software development, robot programming, and sensor calibration. 

Key Contributions:

• Competition Pruning Robot: As the sole Computer Engineering student on the team, I spearheaded the software development for autonomous robots aimed at simulating complex pruning operations. Leveraging Arduino, EV3, and Raspberry Pi platforms, I devised intricate algorithms for navigation, image processing, and communication. My efforts resulted in a robust system capable of selectively cutting and removing plant material, earning recognition for our team's innovation.

• Forage Biomass Robot Concept Design: Collaborating on the conceptualization of an autonomous robot for measuring forage biomass, I devised novel designs integrating load cells, suspensions, and Arduino programming. Additionally, I contributed to the design feedback loop, ensuring optimal performance and lightweight construction for field deployment.

• UAV Sensor Setup and Calibration: Tasked with enhancing the Water Quality Monitoring UAV, I tackled the challenge of integrating new sensors and optimizing data logging processes. Debugging existing Arduino programs and calibrating sensors, I streamlined data collection and analysis, particularly focusing on turbidity sensor calibration and servo control. My meticulous approach ensured the seamless integration of new sensor technologies into the UAV platform.

Throughout these projects, I demonstrated proficiency in Python, LabVIEW, and C++, employing advanced engineering techniques such as PID control for precise navigation and image processing with OpenCV for object detection. My internship at Clemson University has honed my skills in robotics, programming, and sensor integration, providing a solid foundation for my academic and professional pursuits in the field of engineering.

projects.title: NASA Swarmathon Physical Competition
projects.description:
Team leader on NASA Swarmathon Competition for Inter-American University team. This national competition is held by NASA Kennedy Space Center where universities are tasked to develop a swarm of autonomous robots that can search an unknown area as a swarm and collect and deliver resources on unknown locations. This competition simulates what would be a real mission on Mars. 
•	Lead a team of 12 team students
•	Responsible of setting requirements for the team
•	Responsible for setting weekly meetings and keeping up-to-date with all members’ tasks
•	Managed team on building robots
•	Tutored new members of the team
•	Responsible for team’s understanding of the concepts of the competition
•	Analyze the best possible way to solve the challenge
•	Mentored teammates on how to work with the software
•	Main developer for the robots’ communication, coordinate system, fidelity functionality, swarm organization and robots’ smart map distribution
•	Oversaw all physical tests
•	Third place on outreach report

projects.title: ASABE 2017 International Robotics Competition
projects.description:
In the 2017 ASABE International Robotics Competition, my team and I undertook the challenge of designing autonomous robots tasked with pruning raspberry bushes. Our project encompassed a range of responsibilities and innovations:

Challenge:
• Simulate full primocane suppression and selective floricane removal pruning operations autonomously.
• Identify and selectively cut irregularly distributed primocanes and floricanes while clearing debris.

Our Contributions:
• Designed and programmed autonomous robots capable of executing complex pruning tasks with precision.
• Utilized a mix of Arduino, EV3, and Raspberry Pi platforms for software development.
• Implemented Python, C++, and LabVIEW for programming various components of the robots.
• Developed a sophisticated communication system using Bluetooth, I2C, and Serial protocols to coordinate between robot components.
• Provided critical feedback to mechanical and electrical engineers in refining the physical design of the robots.
• Pioneered image processing capabilities leveraging OpenCV for object detection and tracking.
• Engineered navigation systems incorporating PID control for precise movement across varied terrains.
• Conducted extensive testing to ensure the reliability and efficiency of all software features.

Accomplishments:
• Successfully created robots capable of identifying and pruning raspberry canes with precision, meeting the competition's requirements.
• Implemented robust software sequences for automation, enabling seamless operation of the robots.
• Integrated advanced image processing techniques to enhance the robots' ability to detect and prune specific branches accurately.
• Developed a comprehensive navigation system utilizing Mecanum wheels and PID control for omnidirectional movement and obstacle avoidance.

This project showcased our proficiency in software development, engineering design, and problem-solving, demonstrating our ability to innovate and excel in challenging environments.
